walkthrough:
Identify the key features of $y = 3\sin x + 2$ on $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{Midline: } y = 2, \quad \text{Amplitude: } 3, \quad \text{Max: } y = 5 \text{ at } x = \frac{\pi}{2}, \quad \text{Min: } y = -1 \text{ at } x = \frac{3\pi}{2}$$
Sketch a smooth sine wave starting at $(0, 2)$, rising to the peak $(0.5\pi, 5)$, crossing $(1\pi, 2)$, reaching the trough $(1.5\pi, -1)$, and ending at $(2\pi, 2)$.

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Graph Sketch: Draws full period sine wave with midline $2$, maximum $5$ at $\pi/2$, and minimum $-1$ at $3\pi/2$ (B2).

hints: Compare the graph of $y = 3\sin x + 2$ with $y = x$.
walkthrough:
Consider the intersection of $y = 3\sin x + 2$ and the line $y = x$ on $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{At } x = 0:\quad y_{\text{curve}} = 2 > y_{\text{line}} = 0$$
$$\text{At } x = \pi:\quad y_{\text{curve}} = 2 < y_{\text{line}} = \pi \approx 3.14$$
$$\text{For } x \ge \pi:\quad y_{\text{line}} \ge \pi > y_{\text{curve}} \le 2$$

Conclude that the line intersects the curve exactly once:
$$\text{Number of solutions} = 1$$

hints: Compare $y = 5 - x$ with the sine curve across $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
walkthrough:
Examine the intersections of $y = 3\sin x + 2$ with the straight line $y = 5 - x$ on $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{At } x = 0:\quad y_{\text{line}} = 5 > y_{\text{curve}} = 2$$
$$\text{At } x = \frac{\pi}{2}:\quad y_{\text{line}} = 5 - \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 3.43 < y_{\text{curve}} = 5$$
$$\text{At } x = \pi:\quad y_{\text{line}} = 5 - \pi \approx 1.86 < y_{\text{curve}} = 2$$
$$\text{At } x = 2\pi:\quad y_{\text{line}} = 5 - 2\pi \approx -1.28 < y_{\text{curve}} = 2$$

By intermediate value crossings across the peaks and troughs, the line intersects the curve at three distinct points:
$$\text{Number of solutions} = 3$$

hints: Factorise the quadratic in $\sin x$ into $(5\sin x - 2)(\sin x + 1) = 0$.
walkthrough:
Replace $\cos^2 x$ with $1 - \sin^2 x$ in the given equation:
$$3\sin x + 2 = 5(1 - \sin^2 x) - 1 \implies 3\sin x + 2 = 4 - 5\sin^2 x$$

Rearrange into a standard quadratic in $\sin x$:
$$5\sin^2 x + 3\sin x - 2 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic:
$$(5\sin x - 2)(\sin x + 1) = 0 \implies \sin x = 0.4 \quad\text{or}\quad \sin x = -1$$

Solve $\sin x = 0.4$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ in radians:
$$x_1 = \sin^{-1}(0.4) \approx 0.41\text{ rad}$$
$$x_2 = \pi - 0.4115 \approx 2.73\text{ rad}$$

List all solutions in the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$:
$$x = 0.41, \quad 2.73, \quad \frac{3\pi}{2}$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Quadratic Equation: Substitutes $\cos^2 x = 1-\sin^2 x$ (M1), forms $5\sin^2 x + 3\sin x - 2 = 0$ (DM1), finds $\sin x = 0.4, -1$ (A1), and gives $x = 0.41, 2.73, \frac{3\pi}{2}$ (A2).
